# Agatha Sowerby

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c9 P16](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0016), [v1 c9 P31](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0031)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  <sub>[v5 c3 P6](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0006)</sub>
- **Origin:** St. Brendan's Island  <sub>[v2 c1 P48](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0048)</sub>
- **Role:** homemaker and quilt-maker  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v5 c3 P6](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0006)</sub>
- **Titles:** Mrs.  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Agatha Sowerby  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>; Mrs. Agatha  <sub>[v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014)</sub>

## Appearance

Mrs. Agatha Sowerby is a stout, heavy woman weighing two hundred pounds, whose natural gait is a perpetual waddle. She has gentle, aged arms and hand-coarsened hands from a lifetime of hard labor.

_Sources: [v1 c9 P31](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0031), [v1 c38 P30](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0030), [v2 c26 P1](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0001), [v3 c40 P14](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0014)_

## Personality

Mrs. Agatha Sowerby is a devout, candid, and opinionated woman who takes great pride in voicing her thoughts without fear or partiality. Though frequently meddlesome, authoritative, and critical of others, she possesses a deeply kind, generous, and compassionate heart. She is highly industrious and vigilant, maintaining strict order while managing her household and church responsibilities. She holds strong, unyielding prejudices—such as disbelieving in women's higher education and harboring a distrust of Yankees—yet she is willing to admit when her initial judgments prove wrong.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000), [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v1 c10 P33](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0033), [v1 c15 P84](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0084), [v1 c15 P89](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0089), [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043), [v1 c31 P7](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0007), [v1 c36 P32](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0032), [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P48](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0048), [v2 c1 P50](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0050), [v2 c9 P10](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0010), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c26 P0](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0000)_

## History

Living at Sowerby's Hollow in Brierley, Mrs. Agatha Sowerby spent decades as a central figure in the community, leading church societies and keeping a watchful eye over her neighbors. When Nell Harcourt first arrived at Grey Shutters, Mrs. Agatha criticized her appearance, sparking a fierce outburst from Nell; however, after Nell offered a humble apology, Mrs. Agatha quickly forgave her. Over time, she grew fond of Nell and actively assisted her and the Abernethys, including dressmaking for Nell and managing various church events. When her husband Thomas fell sick and died, Mrs. Agatha nursed him devotedly; facing financial hardship and the sale of her farm, she accepted Thirza Abernethy's invitation to move into Grey Shutters rather than leave Brierley. At Grey Shutters, she remained deeply involved in parish affairs and community gossip while helping raise the children. In her later years, she continued to reside at Grey Shutters, occupying her time by crafting cotton-warp quilts for Nell's future daughters.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000), [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v1 c9 P30](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0030), [v1 c10 P33](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0033), [v1 c10 P34](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0034), [v1 c25 P25](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0025), [v2 c14 P5](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0005), [v2 c26 P0](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0000), [v2 c26 P15](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0015), [v2 c26 P26](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0026), [v2 c30 P0](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0000), [v3 c5 P8](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0008), [v5 c3 P6](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0006)_

- raised ten children (losing two) without relying on store catalogues  <sub>[v1 c9 P30](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0030), [v4 c4 P12](../source/v04-c04.md#nw-v04-c04-p0012)</sub>

## Quotes

> Well, they didn’t choose you on account of your appearance, that’s without a doubt. She’s awfully thin and plain, Thirza. Step over this way, child, so I can inspect you. Goodness gracious, has anyone ever witnessed such freckles? And hair that is as red as carrots! Step over this way, child, I tell you.  <sub>[v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014)</sub>

> Come, come, stand up, little one. Naturally, you have my forgiveness. It seems I was likely somewhat overly strict with you, regardless. However, I am simply quite a candid individual. You simply must not pay me any heed, that is all. No one can dispute that your hair is exceedingly red; nevertheless, I used to know a female—we actually attended school together—who possessed hair precisely as red as yours in her youth, yet it deepened into a truly lovely auburn as she matured. It would not amaze me in the slightest if the same thing happened to yours—not in the slightest.  <sub>[v1 c10 P34](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0034)</sub>

> I must say I am becoming pleased to take a seat. My feet have carried me the whole day, and two hundred pounds is quite a weight for just two feet to haul about. Not being overweight is a major blessing, Thirza. I trust you are grateful for it. Now, Nell, word has reached me that you abandoned your plan to attend college. Hearing that made me genuinely pleased. You currently possess as much learning as is good for a woman’s comfort. Girls attending college alongside men and filling their brains with Latin and Greek and such foolishness is something I do not support.  <sub>[v1 c38 P31](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0031)</sub>

> Nell has reached eighteen; I had already wed by the time I was that age. We older people, Thirza, tend far too often to believe that kids remain young forever, that is the truth. Nell is now a grown woman and Hugh has become a man, and he adores the very earth beneath her feet, which is obvious to everyone. He is an excellent gentleman, and Nell could not make a finer match. I trust she will not adopt any foolish romantic ideas while at Wexcombe. I do not endorse those coeducational institutions and never have, that is the truth. I am convinced that those attending such colleges rarely accomplish much beyond flirting.  <sub>[v3 c2 P23](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0023)</sub>

> Without using Eaton’s catalogue, I entertained a total of ten children.  <sub>[v4 c4 P12](../source/v04-c04.md#nw-v04-c04-p0012)</sub>
